newsitem.title: FINLAND: KAUBAMAJA SEES 97 HELSINKI SALES FIM 20 MLN.
newsitem.headline: KAUBAMAJA SEES 97 HELSINKI SALES FIM 20 MLN.

text.p: Estonian retailer Tallinna Kaubamaja sees net sales of 20 million markka and a break-even result for its new Helsinki department store this year, the group's chairman of the board said on Tuesday.

"This year we are aiming for net sales of about 20 million markka," Tallinna Kaubamaja's chairman Toomas Luman told Reuters on the sidelines of a news conference on the eve of the opening of a store in downtown Helsinki, its first outside Estonia.
"This store will not bring us any profit this year ... we've budgeted for a break-even result," Luman said.
"But it will raise our purchasing volume and help make the whole group a more attractive buyer to manufacturers and wholesalers ... That is our goal for this year," he added.
The new store, with about 1,200 square metres of floorspace and more than 20 employees, will open for busines on Wednesday.
It will be operated by Finnish subsidiary Tallinna Kaubamaja Suomi Oy, established in 1996.
The group has invested over 30 million kroons in the Helsinki store, it said in a statement.
Tallinna Kaubamaja operates the Kaubamaja department store in the Estonian capital. In 1996 the group had net sales of 494 million Estonian kroons and a net profit of 28.8 million kroons.
The group aims to increase its net sales to one billion kroons "in a few years" and to two billion kroons in five to eight years, Luman said. ($ = 13.84 kroons)
